transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-29 16:00 PST | Duration: 43m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sara, Diego, Olivia, Marcus (Polaris Beacon)

Summary: quick discovery focused on time-to-first-token (TTFT), free credits for PLG path, and evaluating hosting fit (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC). Customer has a 2-3 month pilot timeline and a security checklist that includes KMS + SOC2.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving the time. quick intro — I'm Maya, I'm the AE working with Polaris Beacon. Liam's our solutions engineer, he'll jump in on the infra and benchmarks. could we do a 1 minute round robin?
[00:12] Sara: sure, sara patel, cto. we're evaluating options for a contextual search assistant and content gen features, want something we can get live quickly.
[00:18] Diego: diego here, lead ml eng. I care about latency tail, token economics, and model reproducibility across environments.
[00:25] Olivia: olivia, s r e — I'll validate networking and security constraints, we have strict egress rules.
[00:31] Marcus: marcus, product, focused on time to ship a demo for execs in 6 weeks.
[00:37] Liam: great, thanks. quick agenda — TTFT and free credits playbook, hosted vs dedicated vs private fit, benchmark approach and next steps. sound good?
[00:44] Sara: yep.

[01:05] Maya: so to start, our PLG path is usually self-serve API with credits. typical flow — we give trial credits, devs sign up, they run a few sample requests, then we help with a short workshop if they hit integration blockers. for Polaris, we can provision 50k trial tokens and a sandbox project. how many devs should we add?
[01:20] Diego: two main engs plus me, so 3. we'd like to run an initial end-to-end using our content pipeline.
[01:27] Maya: perfect. for TTFT — most teams hit first successful call in under an hour with our quickstart (sdk + curl + postman snippets). Liam, you wanna explain the usual hiccups?
[01:35] Liam: yeah, common items — API key rotation, default rate limits, and network egress if you're behind a company firewall. If you use hosted it's literally get key, run sample, done. Dedicated gives predictable throughput but requires a little ops setup. Private VPC/on-prem is heavier — need networking coordination and KMS integration. sometimes our samples assume port 443 egress; if your egress is limited we'll need to open endpoints.
[02:05] Olivia: right — our security team blocks outbound to unknown hosts by default. we'd prefer either VPC peering or a dedicated private endpoint. is that something Redwood supports?
[02:13] Liam: yes — we offer Private deployments with a customer-managed VPC and private endpoints. we also support dedicated capacity with restricted network egress and a private control plane for enterprise. for the PLG trial though, hosted api is the fastest to validate product-market fit.
[02:29] Diego: curious about data retention and logs — we need audit logs for tokens and to show we don't persist PII.
[02:35] Maya: good question. by default hosted retains minimal logs for 30 days; for enterprise we can enable longer retention and customer-managed KMS for model payload encryption. i'll include the exact retention table in the security pack.

[03:00] Marcus: quick question — what's the typical latency we can expect for a 2k token prompt on hosted?
[03:07] Liam: for a medium sized open model, 2k prompt, you should expect median ~250–350ms per token generation step depending on model; end-to-end for full response typically 600–1200ms. there is variance though. on Dedicated GPUs with optimized kernels we see lower tail latencies and higher throughput.
[03:27] Diego: those numbers are helpful. can we run a controlled benchmark showing p50/p95 across a typical prompt distribution?
[03:33] Liam: absolutely — we'll provide a short benchmark script and a spreadsheet for you to populate prompts. that's one of the action items.

[04:05] Maya: also to manage cost, we recommend prefix caching and batching for high-traffic routes. Redwood Optimize — or the doc that Liam will link, "redwood optima" — suggests quantization and batching policies that can cut token cost ~30–60% depending on workload.
[04:23] Diego: hmm ok, we do lots of short prompts, so batching might not help that much. prefix caching could help since many prompts share context.
[04:31] Liam: yes caching KV cache behavior matters. note, sometimes transcription or docs say "K V cache" but it's the kv cache in the runtime. we'll include guidance on serialization and cache warmup.

[05:10] Olivia: on compliance, do you have SOC2 Type II? and what about encryption at rest — can we bring our own KMS?
[05:18] Maya: we do have SOC2 Type II and ISO docs; yes, enterprise/private deployments support BYOK (bring your own key) via KMS integrations, and you can configure the control plane to not persist unencrypted payloads. i'll attach the certs.

[06:00] Marcus: how long to stand up a dedicated pool vs private?
[06:06] Liam: dedicated usually takes a couple of days for provisioning and config for production traffic, shorter for dev/test. private VPC deployments are more like 2–4 weeks depending on network approvals and HSM/KMS provisioning. for a pilot we often start hosted then move to dedicated if throughput or SLOs require it.
[06:25] Sara: that's useful. Our timeline is 6 weeks to demo; pilot start in 4 weeks. sounds like hosted trial fits timeline.

[07:10] Diego: what about model parity — if we go hosted and later move to dedicated or private, are we guaranteed same outputs?
[07:17] Liam: good point. we version models and provide model artifacts; parity is high but differences can occur due to quantization or custom kernels. for strict reproducibility we support pinning model versions and providing rollout notes. we'll also share a reproducibility checklist.
[07:35] Diego: ok, good. also want to run a regression eval against our prompt set during migration.

[08:05] Maya: next up — pricing / credits. for the trial we'll provision 50k tokens and a short credits plan. if you want long-running pilot we can add a reserved monthly commit for dedicated at an enterprise rate. i'll share a simple cost model for hosted vs dedicated.
[08:22] Marcus: can you include example invoices or unit economics? Product wants to show cost per session to execs.
[08:28] Maya: yes, we'll add sample unit economics and an example invoice.

[09:00] Olivia: about SSO — we use SAML and SCIM for provisioning. is that supported for trial accounts?
[09:06] Maya: for trials we usually invite devs via email; SSO and SCIM is part of our enterprise package and can be added when you move to a dedicated/private plan.

[10:00] Liam: small note — if you want to try local dev with low-latency testing, you can use our sandbox region and emulate higher latencies. we'll include postman and node/python sdk examples and a curl template.

[11:30] Diego: any gotchas we should know about when running in a restricted network and using private endpoints?
[11:35] Liam: firewall rules for control plane endpoints, DNS resolution for the private endpoint, and port egress; also KMS endpoints for BYOK must be reachable from the VPC. Olivia, if you share your firewall policy we'll map the exact endpoints.

[13:00] Maya: alright, to recap — we'll: provision trial credits and invite devs, send security docs + SOC2, provide benchmark script + cost model, and schedule a workshop. any additions?
[13:12] Sara: can you also include a short runbook for migrating from hosted to dedicated?
[13:16] Maya: yes, migration runbook will be part of the docs pack.

[14:00] Marcus: ok process wise — who should I look for if we want to accelerate to dedicated?
[14:05] Maya: you'll work with me and Liam; for enterprise onboarding there's a TAM assigned if you go on contract.

[15:20] Diego: question on throttling and quotas — during our spike tests, can we request temporary bursts?
[15:27] Liam: for dedicated pools we can configure burst capacity; in hosted we can often increase limits temporarily but you'd need to coordinate with our ops team.

[16:10] Olivia: from a security checklist perspective, we'll need an architecture diagram and ATO inputs. can you give a high-level diagram?
[16:17] Liam: yes we'll attach a one-page architecture diagram showing hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC flows and where KMS sits.

[17:00] Maya: ok i'll send the security pack and architecture plus trial invite by tomorrow EOD.

[17:20] Sara: great. Diego, any blockers to start once devs have invites?
[17:25] Diego: none on our side; i just need the prompt set and the benchmark script.

[18:00] Maya: last admin — i'll propose a 60m workshop slot next thursday or friday; what works better?
[18:07] Sara: thursday morning is best for us.

[18:30] Maya: noted. we'll target Thursday 10am PT.

[19:00] Marcus: thanks all — very helpful call.
[19:05] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items.

Auto-generated topics: Time-to-first-token (TTFT), Trial credits and onboarding, Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fit, Security compliance (SOC2, KMS, SSO), Benchmarking and cost modeling.
